targetWords.definition: To appeal to someone is to be interesting or attractive to them.
targetWords.example: ■Sleeping all day appeals to me, but I have to go to school. fs

targetWords.definition: To assume something is to think that it is true, even with no proof.
targetWords.example: I assume you are both fam iliar with this plan. f^ borrow [bo(:)rou] v. To borrow something is to take it and then give it back later.

targetWords.definition: A client is a person or business that pays another to do a service.
targetWords.example: She has many clients who enjoy coming to her salon.

targetWords.definition: The downtown is the center of most cities.
targetWords.example: The downtown is filled with many tall buildings.

targetWords.definition: If something is dull, it is not exciting.
targetWords.example: The movie was very dull. I fell asleep watching it.

targetWords.definition: To embarrass someone is to make them feel ashamed or foolish.
targetWords.example: He was embarrassed when he couldn't remember her name.

targetWords.definition: A fare is an amount of money paid to use a bus, train, or taxi.
targetWords.example: ■Since he is a senior, my grandfather pays a low fare for the bus.

targetWords.definition: Former describes something that used to be but is not any more.
targetWords.example: The hotel, a former castle, was built over 200 years ago.

targetWords.definition: A formula is a set mathematical way or method of solving a problem.
targetWords.example: I learned a new formula that may help us with our problem.

targetWords.definition: To found a company or organization means to start it.
targetWords.example: The pilgrims founded one of the first colonies in the United States.

targetWords.definition: To invest means to use money in a way that will bring a profit later.
targetWords.example: I invested money in a new building that should bring me a profit.

targetWords.definition: A loan is the act of lending something, usually money.
targetWords.example: I got a loan from the bank.

targetWords.definition: If something is practical, it is useful in normal life. — Learning English is practical; you can use it in many places.

targetWords.example: ■He paid a quarter for the candy.

targetWords.definition: A salary is how much money a person makes at his or her job.
targetWords.example: He got a new job with a better salary.

targetWords.definition: A scholarship is money given to one so they can go to school.
targetWords.example: I got a scholarship to help me pay for university.

targetWords.definition: If something is temporary, it exists for a short time.
targetWords.example: ■This car is only temporary; I'll get a new one soon.

targetWords.definition: A treasure is a collection of valuable things, especially jewels or gold.
targetWords.example: They became very rich when they found the buried treasure.

targetWords.definition: To urge someone is to try very hard to get them to do something.
targetWords.example: ■He urged them to believe his story.

story.title: The Taxi Driver
story.passage:
Peter's job was driving a taxi downtown. He made a small salary. But he

liked his job because it wasn't dull. Every day, he saw new things that appealed

to him. Peter was practical about the future. " Maybe I can get a scholarship to

college," he thought. " I could learn mathematical formulas and get a job at a

bank. I could help clients invest their money."

Peter stopped to pick up a passenger. "Where to?" he asked.

" Go to the Fourth Street Bank. And don't talk to me. I've had a rough day,"

the man said. Peter was angry, but he had a peaceful philosophy. When they

stopped, the man's fare came to $10.25. He put his hands in his pockets. " I

can't find my wallet!" he said. " I can't pay the fare!"

Peter said, " Maybe I'll give you a temporary loan. You can borrow ten dollars

and a quarter from me."

The man was embarrassed, saying, " I was mean to you, but now I want to

help you. I founded this bank. I want to give you one thousand dollars."

That much money was like a treasure to Peter. The man urged him to take the

money, but he didn't.

"You're an honest person," the man said. " I

assumed you would take it. I want you to work for

me."

The next day, Peter started his job at the bank.

He was happy to be done with his former job.
